dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: At every handover the operator retypes `/model` and `/effort` from the `└ opus · high effort` caption and picks the leg command out of an indented prose block (tests/golden/execute.txt); the user asked for copy-paste blocks instead.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: User confirmed three goals: 0 retyped commands per handover (down from 2), plain CLI prints the NEXT commands one per line without the caption, and select/status/fleet output byte-identical with `--json` state untouched.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: User approved the command checks (suite, markdown tests, caption gone, slash commands pass `--markdown`) plus one desktop-app judgment; the success-criteria critic's fence-shape, unindented-lines, unchanged-golden and flag-conflict checks were folded in.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: User chose `--markdown` echoed by /waybill:next and /waybill:bay; /waybill:new only gets its run-the-leg-command instruction fixed (critic finding); status, the SELECT menu, the release bump and a context-window field are explicitly out.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The user's live paste test (`/model haiku` + newline + `/effort low` → "Model 'haiku     /effort low' not found") resolved the one-block-vs-many conflict in favour of one fence per command, and the user accepted the drafted output as-is.

problem: Waybill's whole job is to hand the next session its orders, but the NEXT block hands them over as prose. The model and effort arrive as a caption — `└ opus · high effort` — that the operator has to translate into `/model opus` and `/effort high` by hand, and `/clear, then run:` fuses an instruction to a sentence. Every leg of every docket pays that translation at the exact moment the operator is switching context.

The obvious fix — one block holding `/model`, `/effort` and the command, as the request sketched it — does not work: Claude Code submits a multi-line paste as one input, so `/model` receives the following lines as its argument. The user's live test returned `Model 'haiku     /effort low' not found`. Each slash command therefore has to be its own paste, which makes one copy button per command the thing worth building.
goals: Every command a handover needs — `/clear` (transfer legs), `/model`, `/effort` (when booked), the leg command, and `cd` (when present) — arrives as its own fenced block in /waybill:next and /waybill:bay: 0 commands retyped per handover, down from 2.
Plain `waybill next` (and `new`, `bay`) prints the NEXT commands one per line, unindented, and the `└ model · effort` caption and `/clear, then run:` line are gone.
No regressions: the SELECT A DOCKET, status, fleet and complete goldens are byte-identical to main, and `--json` is untouched because the change is render-only.

successCriteria.criterion: The full suite passes, including new `.md` goldens for every booked leg.

check.expect: exits 0 (at least one matching test passed)

successCriteria.criterion: In the execute markdown golden, every handover command sits alone between bare fences — `/model` and `/effort` never share a block.

check.cmd: for c in '/clear' '/model opus' '/effort high' '/spec:apply add-thing'; do [ "$(grep -Fx -B1 -A1 -- "$c" tests/golden/execute.md | grep -cx '```')" -eq 2 ] || exit 1; done

successCriteria.criterion: Plain output lists the NEXT commands unindented, one per line, with no `then run:` line left in any golden.

check.cmd: grep -qx '/model opus' tests/golden/execute.txt && grep -qx '/effort high' tests/golden/execute.txt && grep -qx '/spec:apply add-thing' tests/golden/execute.txt && ! grep -q 'the[n].run:' tests/golden/*.txt

successCriteria.criterion: No golden carries the `└ model · effort` caption.
The select, status, fleet and complete goldens are unchanged from main.

check.cmd: git diff --exit-code main -- tests/golden/select.txt tests/golden/status.txt tests/golden/fleet.txt tests/golden/fleet-empty.txt tests/golden/complete.txt

successCriteria.criterion: `--json` with `--markdown` is rejected with exit 2 and an error naming the conflict.

check.cmd: node src/cli.js next --json --markdown >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && node src/cli.js next --json --markdown 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--markdown'

successCriteria.criterion: Both handover slash commands ask the CLI for the markdown form, including the `next <branch>` re-run in /waybill:next's SELECT A DOCKET step.

check.cmd: grep -q 'cli.js" next --markdown' commands/next.md && grep -q 'next --markdown <branch>' commands/next.md && grep -q 'cli.js" bay --markdown' commands/bay.md

successCriteria.criterion: `waybill bay --markdown` puts its `cd` line in a fence of its own.

check.expect: exits 0 (the bay markdown CLI test ran and passed)

successCriteria.criterion: No command file still points the model at the removed `/clear, then run:` handover line.
In a real session the blocks are usable as intended.

check.judgment: The operator runs /waybill:next from a real bay in the Claude desktop app and confirms each command renders as its own code block with a copy button, and that pasting them in order hands off cleanly.

mvp.item: Plain renderer: NEXT lists `/clear` (transfer only), `/model <model>`, `/effort <effort>` (when booked) and the leg command one per line, unindented; the `└` caption and the `/clear, then run:` / `run:` lines are removed; an unrecognised `handover` string is kept as an indented prose line above the commands; the booking body stays indented below; the plain `IN BAY:` cd line is unchanged.
mvp.reason: The commands become the handover itself rather than a caption to translate — goal 2.

mvp.item: `waybill next --markdown`: position block in a ```text fence, a **NEXT** line, a custom handover string as a paragraph, one ``` fence per command in order, `IN BAY:` cd as its own fence, body as unindented prose, IGNORED BY GIT / WARNINGS as bullets.
mvp.reason: One copy button per command is the only shape that survives the paste test — goal 1.

mvp.item: `waybill bay --markdown`: bay renders its own `bay created at …` heading and its cd line in markdown (cd in its own fence) in src/cli.js, using a bare-command form of `cdLines`, then the markdown waybill.
mvp.reason: `bay` prints the cd via its own heading, not the renderer's IN BAY section, so goal 1's fenced cd needs its own path.

mvp.item: commands/next.md and commands/bay.md invoke the CLI with `--markdown`, including next.md's step-2 `next <branch>` re-run; their 'the handover line says whether to /clear' wording points at the `/clear` block instead; the verbatim-echo rule stays.
mvp.reason: Two output modes asked for at once is a caller error, and the CLI already rejects rather than ignores.

mvp.item: commands/next.md and commands/bay.md invoke the CLI with `--markdown`, including next.md's step-2 `next <branch>` re-run, and keep the verbatim-echo rule.
mvp.reason: The model's job stays echo-verbatim; the fences are produced by code a golden can pin.

mvp.item: commands/new.md: of the NEXT block's command lines, run only the last (the leg command) — never `/clear`, `/model` or `/effort`; a commands.test.js assertion pins it.
mvp.reason: new.md's 'ignore the `/clear, then run:` line' instruction targets a line this change removes; left alone, the session could run /clear or /model.

mvp.item: Tests: `assertGolden` gains an extension parameter; every booked-leg `.txt` golden regenerated; a `.md` golden per booked leg plus IN BAY and IGNORED/WARNINGS cases; the hand-written shape assertions in tests/waybill.test.js, booking-swap, bookings-overlay, cli.test.js and commands.test.js updated; markdown tests live in existing suites (or are registered in tests/index.js); README examples updated.
mvp.reason: Golden files are how this repo pins every byte of output.

outOfScope.item: Stopping `/model` and `/effort` from saving as the default for new sessions.
outOfScope.reason: That is Claude Code's behaviour (observed in the user's paste test), not Waybill's; noted, not addressed.
It runs its command in the current session, so there is nothing to paste — though its plain output does change under goal 2, which is why commands/new.md is in MVP.

outOfScope.item: The SELECT A DOCKET menu and `waybill status`.
outOfScope.reason: Neither carries a command for the next session.

outOfScope.item: Placeholders for arguments Waybill cannot supply (e.g. the bay leg's branch name).
outOfScope.reason: A pasted placeholder submits literally; the bare command plus the booking prose is safer.

outOfScope.item: A booking field for context window (e.g. `[1m]`).
outOfScope.reason: `/model opus[1m]` is the documented alias; a booking overlay can say `model: opus[1m]` and it passes through verbatim.
This repo releases in its own `chore: release` PR.

decisions.decision: One fenced block per slash command.
decisions.rejected: One block holding `/model`, `/effort` and the leg command together, as the request sketched it.
decisions.reason: The user's live paste test showed Claude Code submits a multi-line paste as one input: `/model haiku` + newline + `/effort low` returned "Model 'haiku     /effort low' not found".

decisions.decision: Fences only in the slash surface; the plain CLI prints bare, unindented command lines.
decisions.rejected: Emitting ``` fences in the plain CLI output too.
decisions.reason: A plain terminal would show literal backticks around every command.

decisions.decision: A `--markdown` flag on `next` (and `bay`) produces the fenced form; the slash command echoes it verbatim.
decisions.rejected: Having the model wrap each unindented `/` line in a fence per instructions in commands/next.md.
decisions.reason: Model-side transformation cannot be pinned by a golden and drifts between runs.

decisions.decision: Commands with an argument Waybill cannot supply are fenced bare.
decisions.rejected: A placeholder in the fence, e.g. `/waybill:bay feat/<name>`.
decisions.reason: Paste-and-Enter would submit the literal placeholder as a branch name.

decisions.decision: /waybill:next and /waybill:bay switch to markdown; /waybill:new stays plain.
decisions.rejected: Markdown on all three waybill-printing commands.
decisions.reason: /waybill:new runs its command in the current session, so its fences would never be clicked.

decisions.decision: The booking's `model` value is passed to `/model` verbatim.
decisions.rejected: A new booking field for context window to produce forms like `opus5[1m]`.
decisions.reason: Claude Code's documented 1M alias is `opus[1m]`, which a booking can already hold as its `model` value.

decisions.decision: The position block (header + leg strip) goes inside a ```text fence in markdown mode.
decisions.rejected: Leaving it as bare markdown lines.
decisions.reason: Markdown collapses the leg strip's single newlines into one paragraph.

decisions.decision: commands/new.md is updated to run only the leg command.
decisions.rejected: Leaving /waybill:new entirely out of scope (the pre-critic plan).
decisions.reason: Scope-creep and hidden-dependency critics: new.md's skip instruction names the `/clear, then run:` line this change deletes, and the session could run /clear or /model.

decisions.decision: `bay --markdown` renders its own heading and fenced cd in src/cli.js.
decisions.rejected: Relying on the renderer's IN BAY section (the pre-critic plan).
decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic: `bay` never passes cd to renderWaybill and prints `bay created at …` itself, so the renderer's fence could not reach /waybill:bay.

decisions.decision: An unrecognised `handover` string stays as a prose line above the commands; `through` renders nothing, `transfer` renders the `/clear` command.
decisions.rejected: Dropping the handover line for every value.
decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic: custom handovers are printed verbatim on purpose (tests/waybill.test.js 'hand the laptop to Dave', README) and dropping them silently loses a booking's instruction.

decisions.decision: The plain `IN BAY:` / bay cd line keeps its current indented form.
decisions.rejected: Unindenting cd in plain mode too.
decisions.reason: cd is a shell command, not a slash command; the fenced form in markdown mode covers copying, and cli.test.js already pins the indent.

decisions.decision: Success criteria check fence shape, unindented plain lines, unchanged non-waybill goldens and the flag conflict directly.
decisions.rejected: Relying on goldens generated by the same PR plus a single name-pattern test (the pre-critic criteria).
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: UPDATE_GOLDEN rewrites whatever the code prints, so a merged /model+/effort fence would have passed every command check.

phases.title: Paste-ready NEXT block in plain and markdown modes
phases.notes: Single phase: renderer (src/waybill.js), `--markdown` on next and bay plus bay's own markdown heading (src/cli.js), commands/next.md + bay.md + new.md, assertGolden extension parameter, regenerated and new goldens, hand-written shape assertions in five test files, README examples. Rebase note: the in-flight ideation/waybill-help spec edits src/cli.js USAGE, tests/commands.test.js and README.md; whichever lands second rebases those three.
